# HWaveform

> A lightweight signal visualization with CSS motion, pause control, and reduced-motion support.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.9.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HWaveform` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-waveform>`.
- Constructor: `HearthWaveformElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HWaveform.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Decorative signal visualization, not an audio analyser. Values are absolute amplitudes clamped to 0–1; the latest 128 samples are rendered. active enables illustrative CSS motion, with a visible pause/resume control. Reduced motion disables animation entirely. No timers or random values; SSR output is deterministic. Label and state remain available to assistive technology.

## Public API

values: number[] · label: string · active: boolean · height: number

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    values?: number[];
    label: string;
    active?: boolean;
    height?: number;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{
    values: () => [
      0.2, 0.4, 0.7, 0.3, 0.5, 0.9, 0.6, 0.35, 0.8, 0.45, 0.65, 0.25, 0.5, 0.85,
      0.4, 0.7, 0.3, 0.55, 0.95, 0.45, 0.6, 0.8, 0.35, 0.2,
    ],
    height: 80,
  }
```

### Events

update:active(boolean)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:active": [
        active: boolean
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, bars, bar

Use `hearth-waveform::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HWaveform } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HWaveform label="Microphone signal" :values="[0.2,0.5,0.9,0.4,0.7,0.3,0.6,0.8]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-waveform');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Microphone signal",
  "active": false
});

element.addEventListener('update:active', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
